output.headline: Lets two nonpublic special-education schools serve students virtually at no added cost
output.summary: This amends the district’s master contract with nonpublic schools and agencies for two named vendors, La Cheim School and Star Academy. Because of the COVID-19 pandemic, they may deliver services by any means allowed under health orders, including virtually, if the district agrees in writing, and invoices must include more information. There is no additional cost, and all other contract terms stay the same.

vendor.location: El Sobrante, CA; San Rafael, CA
vendor.name: La Cheim School, Inc.; Star Academy

output.headline: Adds $33,000 to keep FM3 Research's bond survey and public opinion work through June 2021

money.evidence: in an additional amount of $33,000.00

output.summary: The district amends its agreement with FM3 Research for survey research, general obligation bond public opinion analysis and communication strategy consulting for the Facilities Planning & Management project. The added $33,000 raises the cap from $33,000 to $66,000, and the end date moves from June 30, 2020 to June 30, 2021.

vendor.name: FM3 Research (Fairbank, Maslin, Maullin, Metz and Associates)

output.headline: Pays MKThink $194,488 for continued support of the district's 2019 Facilities Master Plan

money.evidence: in the amount of $194,488.00

output.summary: MKThink continues to support the 2019 Facilities Master Plan, including project prioritization and asset management planning, and collects and manages cost, condition, lifecycle and seismic data. The amount includes a $16,912.00 contingency. Work runs June 25 to December 31, 2020. Paid from Measure J bond funds.

output.headline: Approves the district joining Pleasanton Unified's student data privacy agreement with Zoom
output.summary: The district approves joining ("piggybacking" onto) an existing California Student Data Privacy Agreement between Pleasanton Unified School District and Zoom, Inc. It sets out each side's duties to protect student data sent to Zoom under the service agreement and lasts as long as that agreement or as long as Zoom holds student data. The text states no dollar amount.

output.headline: Pays Metro Contract Group up to $623,807 for furniture for the new Fremont High building and gym

money.evidence: in the amount of $623,807.00

output.summary: Metro Contract Group was the lowest responsive bidder to deliver furniture for the new Fremont High School Building B and gymnasium, 35 classrooms in all. The amount includes a $20,000.00 contingency. The agreement starts June 25, 2020 and ends no later than October 23, 2020. Paid from Measure J bond funds.

output.headline: Names five firms as a pool for asset management and real property services on unneeded district sites
output.summary: The Board adopts a resolution naming five firms as qualified providers of asset management and real property services. They would help the district handle sites identified in the 2019-20 7-11 Committee process (a district review of sites) that may not be needed for education. No dollar amount is stated.

output.headline: Accepts a $2,505.97 class action settlement award, up $276.54 from the earlier award

money.evidence: an increase of $276.54

output.summary: The district accepts a payment from a class action lawsuit settlement involving Verizon Wireless. The award rises from the $2,229.43 the Board accepted in February 2020 to $2,505.97, an increase of $276.54.

output.headline: Pays New Leaders up to $90,000 in 2019-20 to build school leaders' skills

money.evidence: not to exceed $90,000.00

output.summary: The district hires New Leaders of Oakland, CA to strengthen the skills and capacity of school leaders, under a three-year plan covering 2019-20 through 2021-22. The agreement runs August 1, 2019 through June 30, 2022. The text states a payment limit of $90,000 for the 2019-2020 school year only.

output.headline: Approves Community Day School's 2019-20 School Plan for Student Achievement
output.summary: The Board approves the 2019-2020 School Plan for Student Achievement for Community Day School. This yearly plan sets the school's goals and how it will work toward them. The item states no dollar amount.

output.headline: Pays Rook Electric up to $75,800 to install cameras at Madison Park Academy

money.evidence: in the amount of $75,800.00

output.summary: Rook Electric was the lowest responsive bidder to install 22 new security cameras and connect 20 existing cameras to the Milestone software at Madison Park Academy. The amount includes a $10,000.00 contingency. Work runs June 25 to August 14, 2020. Paid from Measure J bond funds.

output.headline: Adds $75,970 for Oakland Public Education Fund summer student intern stipends

money.evidence: in the additional amount of $75,970.00

output.summary: This amendment adds $75,970 to the contract with the Oakland Public Education Fund, raising the limit from $200,000 to $275,970. The money pays additional stipends to district student interns in the summer career preparation program called ECCCO (Exploring College, Career, and Community Options). It also extends the contract end date from June 30, 2020 to August 7, 2020.

output.headline: Contracts with Raskob Day School for up to $50,000 in 2020-21 special education services

money.evidence: not to exceed $50,000.00

output.summary: The district signs its yearly master contract with Raskob Day School in Oakland, a nonpublic school, to serve students in special education. The district may pay up to $50,000 for the period July 1, 2020 through June 30, 2021. The services are those listed in Section 1 of the contract.

output.headline: Adds $150,000 for more legal services from Lozano Smith, for a $450,000 limit this year

money.evidence: in an additional amount of $150,000.00

output.summary: The law firm Lozano Smith gets $150,000 more to provide legal services as needed, raising its limit for the 2019-20 fiscal year to $450,000. The original agreement is a memorandum of understanding and engagement policy, which is a paid services agreement. All other terms stay the same.

output.headline: Adopts the Board of Education's 2020-21 Governance Handbook
output.summary: The Board adopts its governance handbook for the 2020-21 school year. The item lists no cost.

output.headline: Applies for $318,420 in state Workability 1 funds for job-readiness help for students with disabilities

money.evidence: in the amount of $318,420.00

output.summary: The Board approves the district's Special Education Local Plan Area (SELPA) application to the California Department of Education for $318,420 for 2020-21. The money would support work-readiness skills in the curriculum, career and vocational assessments, pre-job training workshops and employment opportunities for students in special education. If the grant is awarded in whole or in part, the item also authorizes the district to accept it.

output.headline: Reappoints five members of the Measures A, B and J school facilities bond oversight committee
output.summary: The Board ratifies the Board President's reappointment of five eligible members to the committee that oversees school facilities bond spending (Measures A, B and J). Each term ends June 10, 2022.

output.headline: Adopts Measure G1 middle school grants and education spending plans totaling $3,916,012 for 2020-21

money.evidence: in the cumulative amount of $3,916,012.00

output.summary: The Board adopts a resolution approving 2020-21 Measure G1 grant awards and education spending plans for district and charter middle schools, as recommended by the Measure G1 oversight commission. The cumulative amount is $3,916,012.00.

output.headline: Approves new or revised job descriptions for more than 20 district positions
output.summary: The Board adopts Resolution No. 1920-2037 creating or revising job descriptions for more than 20 positions across Nutrition Services, Buildings and Grounds, Linked Learning, Technology, Equity, Early Childhood Education, Police Services and Talent/Human Resources, among others. Examples include a plumber's helper, a production cook, student information systems specialists and a school gardens program manager. The text gives no dollar amount.

output.headline: Amends the 2020-21 classified staff layoffs, reinstatements and new positions resolution
output.summary: The Board adopts Resolution No. 1920-2026B, which amends the list of classified (non-teaching) positions to be cut, brought back, increased or created for 2020-21. The text says the changes reflect lack of funds or program need as shown in the 2020-21 budget process. It gives no dollar amount.

output.headline: Hires Waste Management for trash, recycling and compost service, up to $3,250,000 a year
output.summary: The district signs a general services agreement with Waste Management of Alameda County, Inc. for solid waste, recycling and composting collection, including roll-off services, at the rates in the agreement's Exhibit B. Spending is capped at $3,250,000 per year, and there are two one-year options to extend if both sides agree in writing.

vendor.name: Waste Management of Alameda County, Inc.

output.headline: Revises the 2020-21 school calendar to add an Oakland Educator Wellness Day on May 10, 2021
output.summary: The Board approves a revised 2020-21 school-year calendar. It adds an Oakland Educator Wellness Day on May 10, 2021, a non-duty day for 10-month school site employees, and sets marking period dates.

output.headline: Pays SchoolMint up to $198,500 for school enrollment application, lottery and registration software in 2020-21

money.evidence: not to exceed $198,500.00

output.summary: The district signs a software-as-a-service agreement with SchoolMint for hosting, maintenance, upgrades and support of its School Finder products for choice applications, the lottery and registration, including a data exchange with the Aeries student system. It runs July 1, 2020 to June 30, 2021 and costs no more than $198,500.

output.headline: Directs how the Board casts its ballot in the 2020 CSBA Delegate Assembly runoff election
output.summary: The Board adopts a resolution telling the Board Secretary how to vote in the 2020 California School Boards Association (CSBA) Delegate Assembly runoff for Sub-Region 7-B (Alameda County). The ballot must be returned by August 11, 2020.
